entries.german:
Nicolaus II. dux Oppavice profitetur, se a Johanne, rege Bohemice, ducatum Oppaviensem feudi nomine recepisse et fidelitatis juramentum prcestitisse. Dt. Pragc e V. Nonas Julii 1318.

CXXXVI. Aos Nicolaus Dei gracia Dux Oppavie ad imiversorum tam presentium quam futurorum notitiam cupimus pervenire quod cum Serenissimus Princeps Dominus noster Joannes Boemie et Polonie Rex ac Lucemburgensis Comes Illustris consideratis fidei et servitiorum nostrorum meritis quibus nos sue munifice liberalitatis graciam meruisse cognovit ac pensatis utilibus et fidelibus per nos sibi prestitis et prestandis servitiis ex sua munifica liberalitate nobis et heredibus nostris in feudum et Jure feudi contulerit in perpetuum Terram seu Ducatum suum Oppaviensem cum dignitate et titulo Ducatus ipsius nec non cum Civi- tatibus Castris Munitionibus Villis possessionibus et universis aliis pertinentiis Utilitatibus proventibus et Juribus Terre seu Ducatus ipsius prout in Privilegio suo super ipsis nobis dato hec omnia plenius et expressius continentur, nos pro nobis et pro heredibus nostris recipientes in feudum a dicto Domino nostro Rege ipsum Ducatum cum omnibus et singulis supradictis sibi recipienti pro se et suis heredibus ac successoribus Regibus Bohemie tan- quam vero feudi predicti Domino fecimus et facimus homagium, Promittentes ipsi fidelitatem devotionem obedientiam ac reverentiam perpetuam per presentes corporali per nos interposito Juramento, ordinando et omnino fieri volendo, ut heredes et successores nostri in ipso feudo seu Ducatu succedentes de manibus ejusdem Domini nostri Regis et predictorum suorum idem feudum seu ducatum recipere Jure feudali ac eis homagium fidelitatem devotionem et obedientiam ic reverentiam predictas interposito etiam Juramento promptere ac similiter facere in perpetuum teneantur, obligando nihilominus nos heredes et successores nostros predictos sub premisso Juramento corporaliter prestito solemni stipulatione interposita ipsi Domino nostro Regi heredibus et successoribus suis prefatis promittimus quod quotiescunque et quandocunque ipse Dominus noster Rex jusserit et ejus jusserint successores et eos jurabimus et juvari volumus per heredes et successores nostros contra omnem hominem fideliter toto posse, tanquam ejus fidelis Vasallus nec non ad omnia alia et singula in per petuum que Jura Feudi exigunt et requirunt sed etiam que quisque Vasallus suo vero Domino facere potest in omnibus atque debet: hoc autem specialiter expresso quod si nos et quem- eunque ex nostris heredibus et successoribus nobis succedentibus in Ducatu predicto continget decedere filiis legitimis non relictis exlunc statim Ducatus ipse cum omnibus et singulis supra dictis ad dictum Dominum nostrum Regem ac heredes et successores suos predictos et ad Regnum predictum libere revertalur. Promisimus denique et promittimus solemni inter posita stipulatione ut premissum est pro nobis heredibus ac successoribus nostris predictis sub prestito Juramento predicta omnia et singu'a predictorum firmiter servare perpetuo et inviolabiliter adimplere. Testes autem qui premissis interfuerunt ad hoc rogati et vocati sunt hi: videlicet Illustres Domini Principes Boleslaus et Hyncko Duces Zlesie: nobiles Viri: Ulricus Comes de Hanaw: Otto de Bolandia: Petrus de Rosenberg summus Camerarius Regni Boemie: Ulricus de Mendico Eurggravius Pragensis: Benessius de Wartemberg Pincerna 109 et Hermannus de Miliczin Dapifer dicti Regni: Ulricus de Ryzano Judex Terre: Tyncko de Koldiz: Henricus de Lüchtenburg: Hermannus et frater suus Hyncko filii Pothonis de Frid- land: Bernhardus de Cymmenburch Ensifer: Plichta de Adlar: Hermannus de Swiritz: Joannes Scamborius dictus de Schiltherg: Sbinco de Mendico: Spaczmannus de Benessow: Zezema de Hirstain et Zdenko Kovan. In cujus rei testimonium presentes litteras fieri fecimus et sigilli nostri appensione muniri. Datum Prage V. JVon. Julii Anno Domini 1318. (Excussum apud Sommersberg Silesiacarum rcrum scriptores I. p. 840. Dobner habet in Monument. IV. p. 287. tantum extract.) t
entries.english:
Nicholas II, Duke of Opava, declares that he has received the Duchy of Opava as a fief from John, King of Bohemia, and has sworn an oath of fealty. Issued at Prague on 3 July 1318.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen. We, Nicholas, by the grace of God Duke of Opava, wish it to be known to all, present and future, that since the most serene prince, our lord John, King of Bohemia and Poland and illustrious Count of Luxembourg, having considered the merits of our loyalty and services, by which he recognized that we had deserved the favor of his munificent liberality, and having weighed the useful and faithful services rendered and to be rendered by us to him, has, out of his munificent liberality, granted to us and our heirs in fief and under feudal law, in perpetuity, his land or Duchy of Opava, with the dignity and title of that duchy, and also its cities, castles, fortifications, villages, possessions, and all other appurtenances, benefits, revenues, and rights of that land or duchy, as all these matters are more fully and explicitly set out in his charter given to us concerning them: therefore, we, receiving in fief from the said lord our king, for ourselves and our heirs, the duchy with all and each of the aforesaid things, have done and do homage to him, who receives it for himself and his heirs and successors as Kings of Bohemia, as the true lord of the aforesaid fief. By these presents, with an oath taken by us in person, we promise him perpetual fidelity, devotion, obedience, and reverence. We direct and wholly require that our heirs and successors who inherit this fief or duchy shall likewise be bound in perpetuity to receive that same fief or duchy under feudal law from the hands of the same lord our king and his aforesaid successors, and, likewise under oath, to promise and render to them the aforesaid homage, fidelity, devotion, obedience, and reverence.

Furthermore, binding ourselves and our aforesaid heirs and successors under the oath sworn in person above, by solemn stipulation we promise to that lord our king and his aforesaid heirs and successors that whenever and wherever that lord our king or his successors shall command, we shall faithfully, with all our might, make war against every person, and shall have our heirs and successors do so, as his faithful vassal; and we shall in perpetuity perform all other and each of the things that feudal law requires and demands, as well as all that any vassal can and ought to do in every respect for his true lord. This is expressly stipulated: if it should happen that we or any of our heirs or successors who succeed us in the aforesaid duchy die without leaving legitimate sons, then immediately that duchy, with all and each of the aforesaid things, shall freely revert to the aforesaid lord our king and his aforesaid heirs and successors, and to the aforesaid kingdom.

Finally, as stated above, by solemn stipulation made under oath, we promise for ourselves and our aforesaid heirs and successors firmly to observe and inviolably fulfil all the aforesaid matters and each of them forever.

The witnesses who were present at the foregoing and were requested and summoned for this purpose are: the illustrious lords and princes Boleslaus and Hyncko, dukes of Silesia; the noble men Ulrich, Count of Hanau; Otto of Bolandia; Peter of Rosenberg, highest chamberlain of the Kingdom of Bohemia; Ulrich of Mendico, burgrave of Prague; Benessius of Wartemberg, cupbearer of the said kingdom; Ulrich of Ryzano, judge of the land; Tyncko of Koldiz; Henry of Lüchtenburg; Hermann and his brother Hyncko, sons of Pothon of Friedland; Bernhard of Cymmenburch, standard-bearer; Plichta of Adlar; Hermann of Swiritz; Joannes Scamborius, called of Schiltherg; Sbinco of Mendico; Spaczmannus of Benessow; Zezema of Hirstain; and Zdenko Kovan. In witness of this matter, we have caused these present letters to be made and secured with the impression of our seal. Given at Prague on 3 July in the year of the Lord 1318.
